Heard Sri Upendra Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Imran Khan, learned
Aga, for the State.

2.  The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.123 of 2023, under Sections 498A and 304B IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Jahanabad, District Pilibhit during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was performed with the sister of the informant about one and half years before and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured the deceased, i.e., sister of the informant for want of Rs.Two Lacs and on 9.4.2023 informant received an information that applicant and his family members committed the murder of his sister.

5. He further submtis that actually after marriage deceased conceived twice with applicant but unfortunately both the times her pregnancy was terminated due to her miscarriage and only due to this reason she started living under depression and under deep depression she committed suicide by hanging herself.
6. He further submits that in paragraphs no.13 and 14 of the affidavit filed in support of the instant bail application applicant has taken this specific plea and along with the instant bail application medical prescription and other medical documents of the deceased have been annexed.
7.
He further submits that post mortem report of the deceased also suggests that she died due to hanging and her hyoid bone was found intact.
8. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since11.4.2023.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayerfor bail and submits that applicant is the husband of the deceased and his wife died within 1-1/2 years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but he could not dispute the fact that from the perusal of the documents it reflecrts that deceased was under medical treatment and she was also having pregnancy and in paragraphs no.13 and 14 of the affidavit filed in support of the instant bail application applicant has made specific averment that twice due to miscarriage her pregnancy was terminated.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, applicant is the husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but from the perusal of the post mortem report it appears that she died due to hanging.

12. As per applicant, as after marriage deceased conceived with applicant twice but both the times due to miscarriage here pregnancy was terminated and, therefore, she committed suicide by hanging herself.
13. Further, along with the instant bail application medical prescription and other medical documents have been annexed by applicant.
14. The defence taken by applicant cannot be completely brushed aside at this stage.
15. Applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter is in jail since April, 2023, i.e., for almost 6 months.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
17. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

18. Let the applicant-Mukesh Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
19. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

20. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
